add.issue.name: A goal closes when its tickets are all closed, and leaves the board for a closed list

edit.description.md:
A finished goal stays on the board as a pill forever; the only way out is removing it, which tombstones it and costs its history.

- A goal with tickets, all closed, is closed. Derived, no new event: reopening a ticket or adding one reopens it.
- Done-lane tickets don't count: a goal at 100% in Done keeps its pill until the release closes them.
- Closed goals leave the board's strip.
- Manage goals shows them as a closed list; each opens the goal's panel.
- Filtering by a goal that closes doesn't strand the board; Manage goals stays reachable.
- MCP: `epiq_goal_list` marks closed goals. TUI checked.

add.issue.name: Release binaries crash on start since Ink 8: the SEA patch turns import.meta.resolve into a syntax error

edit.description.md:
Since #546 (Ink 8), `epiq --version` from `npm run build:binary` fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '.'`, on macOS and Windows. Ink's reconciler calls `import.meta.resolve('react-devtools-core')`. build-sea.mjs rewrites bare `import.meta` to `{url:…}`, and at the start of a statement that parses as a block.

Fix: make the stand-in a parenthesised object whose `resolve` throws, so Ink treats devtools as absent (they are stubbed in the binary anyway).

Found by the temporary Windows probe. The binaries are built only on tags, so the next release would have shipped broken.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: build-sea.mjs now replaces bare import.meta with a parenthesised stand-in whose resolve throws, so Ink treats devtools as absent and the binary starts again. Merged in #549. The test that would catch this is CGT7K4R.

add.issue.name: On Node older than 22, epiq exits with a clear message instead of crashing

edit.description.md:
Since #546 (Ink 8), epiq needs Node ≥ 22. `engines` only warns at install, so on Node 18 or 20 the npm install, npx and MCP crash at runtime with an unrelated error. Ubuntu 24.04's apt Node is 18.

Fix: a check at the very start of the CLI and MCP entries. It prints the required and found versions, points to a newer Node or the release binary, and exits 1. The release binary carries its own Node and always passes.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: render() passes interactive from stdout's TTY, so a shell that exports CI still gets the TUI. An e2e test launches with CI=true. Merged in #551.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: lib/utils/node-version.ts runs first in the CLI and MCP entries, from a chunk that Node 18 parses. On Node older than 22 it prints the required and found versions, points to a newer Node or the release binary, and exits 1. Merged in #551.

add.issue.name: A ticket's Code tab takes seconds to list its commits on a long history

edit.description.md:
jola: "Loading commits…" on a ticket's Code tab is very slow, with a large repo connected.

Cause: getCommitsForRef read every source's whole history with `git log --shortstat`, so git diffed every commit ever made, then filtered for the ref in memory. The board's own repo was cached for only 5 seconds.

Fix: git filters by the ref (`--grep`, fixed strings, case-insensitive) and the exact subject and Epiq-Ref rule narrows the result. A hash-only walk supplies each commit's predecessor. A clone's reads are cached per ref set until its next fetch, like its full scan.

add.issue.name: Diff totals on cards take seconds to appear: every commit in history is diffed to sum a few tickets

edit.description.md:
jola: the diff pills on tickets take forever to show up.

Cause: getRefDiffTimeline summed per-ticket totals from the full commit timeline scan, `git log --shortstat` over every commit of every source. In a big repo most of that history names no ticket.

Fix: a walk without diffs finds the commits that name a ticket, by subject lead or Epiq-Ref, and only those are diffed with `--no-walk --stdin --shortstat`. Cached as the full scan is, keeping copied strings. On a 30k-commit repo where 2% name a ticket: 315ms against 1270ms, with identical totals.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: ticket diff totals no longer diff every commit in history. A walk without diffs finds the commits that name a ticket, through namesATicket in lib/commits, and only those get `--no-walk --stdin --shortstat`. The result is cached like the full scan, as copied strings. On a 30k-commit repo where 2% name a ticket: 315ms against 1270ms, with identical totals. A real-git test pins parity with the full scan. Merged in #563.
